checks: The contact tightness normalizes the tilted rows, and multiplying the row mixture by L gives dm/M. The expectation of U/L in a tilted row uses the original row mean of U, so both Jensen inequalities have the stated orientation.

All positive rows and their tilts are dominated by mixed volume up to a finite factor. Fiber boundaries have zero mass. For the nonnegative integrable case each mark has positive U and each row has finite log integral. In the equality case the two row gaps and the nonpositive bound all vanish, giving U/L=1 on the mixture. Continuity and positive volume on each nonempty relatively open part of a full-dimensional fiber give equality on closed fibers.

A positive constant gives a finite lower bound at every positive b. The certificate upper bound, mixing of approximate optimizers, inclusion of feasible sets and scalar rescaling prove the finite concave value, monotonicity, and scaling law. L attains zero, and log x ≤ x−1 gives the certificate-to-supergradient inclusion.

One-sided coordinate increments and the two signs of the scaling test give g≥0 and g·l=1. L+tf is a feasible concave variation at its own marked values for small positive t, and bounded f and a positive minimum of L justify differentiating the integral. Both affine signs give equal mass and all affine-coordinate first moments. Testing minus every continuous convex function gives the required convex order on C.

The measurable allocation set is closed and convex in the Hilbert-space norm, hence weakly closed, and bounded. Its weakly continuous moment map has compact convex image. Strict separation would produce the affine scores with the wrong inequality, since the measurable first-maximizer allocation attains the integral of their maximum and that maximum is an admissible convex test. This works even if two mark labels denote the same point. The probabilities recovered from the desired labeled moments have the right barycenters. Jensen and equality of the total L moments force every positive row to be tight.

The superdifferential is a closed convex set and is bounded by local Lipschitz continuity. Comparing supporting inequalities at l and l+th gives the minimum over old supergradients by local boundedness and the closed graph. Local Lipschitz continuity also absorbs the o(t) perturbation.

overlap.comparison: Both formulas minimize a first-order response over a compact old set. The accepted set consists of hinge minimizers for one retained-mass problem, with a moving mark and a nested body path. Its response gives no fixed-body log-entropy superdifferential for multiple marked upper bounds.

readability: The proof uses two measures on each positive row. The original row supplies its mean and Jensen for U, while its L-tilt supplies log Jensen and the mixture dm/M.
